metadata.title: Organic Chemistry Comprehensive Data
metadata.description: Detailed organic chemistry reference covering hydrocarbons, functional groups, reaction mechanisms, stereochemistry, and spectroscopy. Complements elements.json structure with nested objects and arrays.
metadata.source: IUPAC nomenclature and standard organic textbooks

hydrocarbons.name: methane
uses: chemical feedstock for methanol and chloroform
hydrocarbons.description: Simplest alkane, tetrahedral, non-polar, major greenhouse gas 25x CO2 over 100 years. Undergoes free-radical halogenation and combustion.

hydrocarbons.name: ethane
uses: petrochemical feedstock for ethene via cracking
hydrocarbons.description: Two-carbon alkane showing rotational barrier (~12 kJ/mol) between staggered and eclipsed conformations. Classic Newman projection example.

hydrocarbons.name: propane
uses: LPG fuel for heating and cooking
hydrocarbons.description: Three-carbon alkane, easily liquefied under pressure. Shows no isomerism; first alkane to demonstrate conformational isomerism via rotation.

hydrocarbons.name: butane
hydrocarbons.description: Four-carbon straight-chain alkane, exhibits chain isomerism with 2-methylpropane (isobutane). Anti and gauche conformers differ by 3.8 kJ/mol.

hydrocarbons.name: 2-methylpropane
hydrocarbons.description: Branched isomer of butane, more stable (ΔHf lower by ~7 kJ/mol) and higher octane number. Tertiary carbon demonstrates carbocation stability.
reactions: formation of tert-butyl carbocation: (CH3)3CH + H+ -> (CH3)3C+ + H2

hydrocarbons.name: pentane
hydrocarbons.description: Five-carbon alkane with three chain isomers (n-pentane, isopentane, neopentane). Demonstrates boiling point trend with branching (36.1 vs 9.5°C for neopentane).

hydrocarbons.name: cyclohexane
hydrocarbons.description: Classic cycloalkane, strain-free chair (and twist-boat) conformations, axial/equatorial positions interconvert via ring flip (ΔG‡ ~45 kJ/mol).
reactions: oxidation to adipic acid with HNO3

hydrocarbons.name: ethene
uses: polyethylene production (world's most produced organic compound)
hydrocarbons.description: Simplest alkene, C=C bond 134 pm, rotational barrier ~270 kJ/mol, pi bond reactive to electrophiles. Planar geometry 121.7° H-C-H angle.

hydrocarbons.name: propene
hydrocarbons.description: Second simplest alkene, demonstrates Markovnikov's rule (addition of HX gives 2-halopropane). Allylic position more reactive to radical halogenation.
reactions: peroxide effect: anti-Markovnikov with HBr/ROOR -> CH2Br-CH2-CH3

hydrocarbons.name: but-2-ene
hydrocarbons.description: First alkene to show cis-trans (E/Z) isomerism. Cis isomer less stable by ~4 kJ/mol than trans due to steric strain. Classic for stereochemistry teaching.
reactions: cis -> trans isomerization with I2 catalyst
addition of Br2 anti-addition gives racemic 2,3-dibromobutane

hydrocarbons.name: 1,3-butadiene
hydrocarbons.description: Conjugated diene with delocalised pi electrons, s-cis/s-trans conformers, 15 kJ/mol resonance stabilization. Undergoes both 1,2- and 1,4-addition.

hydrocarbons.name: ethyne
uses: vinyl chloride and acrylic acid synthesis
hydrocarbons.description: Simplest alkyne, linear 180°, triple bond 120 pm, acidic terminal H (pKa ~25) can be deprotonated by NaNH2. Highly endothermic ΔHf=227 kJ/mol, explosive under pressure.

hydrocarbons.name: propyne
hydrocarbons.description: Terminal alkyne, tautomerizes to allene (propa-1,2-diene) under base. More acidic than alkanes/alkenes; forms acetylide anions for C-C bond formation.

hydrocarbons.name: benzene
hydrocarbons.structure: planar hexagon, 6 pi electrons, Hückel aromatic
uses: solvent (less used now due to carcinogenicity)
hydrocarbons.description: Archetypal aromatic hydrocarbon, resonance energy 150 kJ/mol, C-C bond 139 pm intermediate between single/double. Planar, 120° angles, delocalized 4n+2 pi electrons.

hydrocarbons.name: methylbenzene
hydrocarbons.description: Alkylbenzene, activating ortho/para director in EAS due to hyperconjugation. Benzylic C-H (pKa ~41) weaker than aromatic; undergoes side-chain oxidation to benzoic acid with KMnO4.

hydrocarbons.name: naphthalene
hydrocarbons.structure: two fused benzene rings, 10 pi electrons
hydrocarbons.description: Simplest fused PAH, resonance energy 255 kJ/mol, reacts more readily than benzene at alpha position. Sublimes readily; characteristic strong odor.
reactions: sulfonation reversibly at 60°C (kinetic) vs 160°C (thermodynamic alpha vs beta)

hydrocarbons.name: 2-methyl-1,3-butadiene
uses: terpene building block in biology (isoprene rule)
hydrocarbons.description: Biologically crucial diene, building block of terpenes, carotenoids, cholesterol via isopentenyl pyrophosphate. Dimerizes slowly at room temp.

hydrocarbons.name: cyclopropane
hydrocarbons.description: Most strained cycloalkane, angle strain 27.6 kJ/mol per CH2, total strain 115 kJ/mol. Walsh orbitals; behaves somewhat like alkene (adds Br2).
reactions: hydrogenation requires catalyst but more exothermic than normal

functionalGroups.name: alkane
functionalGroups.description: Saturated hydrocarbon with only sigma bonds, non-polar, unreactive except radical halogenation and combustion. Parent for IUPAC naming.

functionalGroups.name: alkene
functionalGroups.description: Contains carbon-carbon double bond (one sigma + one pi). Planar, undergoes electrophilic addition, Markovnikov regioselectivity.

functionalGroups.name: alkyne
functionalGroups.description: Contains carbon-carbon triple bond, linear, acidic terminal hydrogen, undergoes nucleophilic addition and acetylide formation.

functionalGroups.name: alcohol
functionalGroups.description: Hydroxyl group bound to saturated carbon. Polar, H-bonding gives high bp. Primary/secondary/tertiary classification determines oxidation products.

functionalGroups.name: phenol
functionalGroups.irAbsorption: O-H stretch 3200-3600, C-O stretch 1230, aromatic C-H 3030
functionalGroups.description: Hydroxyl directly on aromatic ring, more acidic than aliphatic alcohols due to resonance stabilization of phenoxide. Activating strongly for EAS.

functionalGroups.name: ether
functionalGroups.description: Oxygen bonded to two carbons, relatively inert, good solvent for Grignard reagents. Can form peroxides on storage.

functionalGroups.name: aldehyde
functionalGroups.description: Carbonyl with one H, easily oxidized to acid, undergoes nucleophilic addition, aldol condensation, and Wittig reaction.

functionalGroups.name: ketone
functionalGroups.nmrShift: 1H alpha to C=O 2.1-2.3 ppm, 13C C=O 205-220 ppm
functionalGroups.description: Carbonyl bonded to two carbons, less reactive than aldehydes, no oxidation by Tollens, undergoes Grignard addition to tertiary alcohols.

functionalGroups.name: carboxylic acid
functionalGroups.description: Carboxyl group combines carbonyl and hydroxyl, acidic due to resonance-stabilized carboxylate. Highest priority for suffix naming.

functionalGroups.name: ester
functionalGroups.description: Derived from acid and alcohol, pleasant odors in many fragrances, hydrolyzed by acid/base to acid+alcohol, Claisen condensation.

functionalGroups.name: amine
functionalGroups.description: Derived from ammonia, basic due to lone pair, classified primary/secondary/tertiary. Undergoes alkylation, acylation, diazotization (primary aromatic).

functionalGroups.name: amide
functionalGroups.description: Carboxylic acid derivative with nitrogen, resonance gives planarity and high rotational barrier (15-20 kcal). Neutral but weak acid/base.

functionalGroups.name: nitrile
functionalGroups.description: Contains carbon-nitrogen triple bond, linear, hydrolysed to acid/amide, reduced to amine, polar aprotic solvent.

functionalGroups.name: haloalkane
functionalGroups.description: Carbon-halogen bond polarized, good leaving groups (except F), substrate for SN1/SN2/E1/E2.

functionalGroups.name: thiol
functionalGroups.description: Sulfur analog of alcohol, more acidic, easily oxidized to disulfides (S-S), characteristic strong odor, metal binding.

functionalGroups.name: sulfide (thioether)
functionalGroups.description: Sulfur ether analog, nucleophilic, oxidized to sulfoxide and sulfone, methionine side chain.

functionalGroups.name: epoxide
functionalGroups.description: Three-membered cyclic ether, high ring strain (~114 kJ/mol), undergoes ring opening by nucleophiles regio- and stereospecifically (anti).

functionalGroups.name: nitro
functionalGroups.description: Strong electron-withdrawing group, deactivating meta-director for EAS, easily reduced to amine, alpha-H acidic due to -I effect.

mechanisms.name: SN1 (Unimolecular Nucleophilic Substitution)
mechanisms.rateLaw: Rate = k [substrate]; nucleophile not in rate-determining step
mechanisms.substratePreference: tertiary > secondary (benzylic/allylic) >> primary; requires stable carbocation
mechanisms.nucleophile: weak nucleophiles ok (H2O, ROH); rate insensitive to nucleophile strength
mechanisms.leavingGroup: best: I- > Br- > Cl- >> F- ; sulfonates excellent (OTs, OMs)
mechanisms.solvent: polar protic (H2O, MeOH, EtOH, AcOH) stabilizes carbocation
mechanisms.stereochemistry: racemization if chiral center becomes planar carbocation; partial retention via ion pair
mechanisms.carbocationRearrangement: common: hydride and methyl shifts to more stable carbocation
mechanisms.energyProfile: two energy barriers: ionization (slow, rate-determining) then nucleophilic capture (fast)
mechanisms.conditions: low nucleophile concentration, heat, protic solvent

steps.name: Ionization / Carbocation Formation
steps.description: C-X bond heterolysis with leaving group departure, forming planar sp2 carbocation. Rate-determining; solvent-assisted. Slow step requires activation energy 60-90 kJ/mol.
steps.arrow: C-Br bond electrons go to Br- ; (CH3)3C+ forms
steps.stereochemistry: chiral substrate loses configuration -> planar achiral intermediate

steps.name: Nucleophilic Attack
steps.description: Weak nucleophile (H2O) attacks empty p orbital from either face with equal probability. Fast, low barrier.
steps.arrow: lone pair of O (H2O) -> empty p orbital of C+
steps.stereochemistry: attack from both faces -> racemate if applicable

steps.name: Deprotonation
steps.description: Base (water or Br-) removes extra proton to give neutral alcohol. Very fast proton transfer.

sideReactions: E1 elimination competes (especially at higher temperature)
mechanisms.howToFavour: use tertiary substrate, weak nucleophile, polar protic solvent, poor base, low temperature disfavours elimination

mechanisms.name: SN2 (Bimolecular Nucleophilic Substitution)
mechanisms.substratePreference: methyl > primary > secondary >> tertiary (no reaction); benzylic/allylic accelerated
mechanisms.nucleophile: strong nucleophiles favoured; anionic > neutral; I- > Br- > Cl- > F- in aprotic solvent
mechanisms.leavingGroup: same as SN1; better leaving group accelerates both
mechanisms.solvent: polar aprotic (DMSO, DMF, acetone, MeCN) enhances nucleophilicity by not H-bonding to anion
mechanisms.stereochemistry: complete inversion (Walden inversion) via backside attack; 100% stereospecific
mechanisms.energyProfile: single transition state, concerted, pentacoordinate [Nu---C---X]‡ with 90° H-C-H and 180° Nu-C-X
mechanisms.conditions: high nucleophile concentration, polar aprotic solvent, unhindered substrate

steps.name: Concerted Backside Attack and Leaving Group Departure
steps.description: Nucleophile lone pair attacks sigma* antibonding orbital from 180° opposite leaving group, simultaneously as C-X bond breaks. Single transition state, no intermediate, trigonal bipyramidal geometry.
steps.arrow: HO- lone pair -> C sigma* (C-Br), Br- leaves with bonding electrons
steps.intermediate: none; transition state [HO---CH3---Br]‡ with partial bonds
steps.stereochemistry: umbrella flip; R->S inversion; if attacked at achiral center, no stereochemical label but mechanism still backside

sideReactions: E2 elimination competes with hindered bases or at higher temp
never competes with SN1 on same substrate under ideal conditions
mechanisms.howToFavour: methyl/primary substrate, strong anionic nucleophile, polar aprotic solvent, low temperature

mechanisms.name: E1 (Unimolecular Elimination)
mechanisms.base: weak base (H2O, alcohol, halide); strong base drives E2 instead
mechanisms.leavingGroup: same as SN1; stable carbocation needed
mechanisms.stereochemistry: no strict anti-periplanar required for C-H cleavage (carbocation planar); Zaitsev product major (more substituted alkene)
mechanisms.carbocationRearrangement: common; most stable alkene formed but rearranged carbocation can shift double-bond position
mechanisms.energyProfile: two barriers: ionization then proton abstraction from carbocation
mechanisms.conditions: heat favours elimination over substitution (ΔS positive), weak base, polar protic

steps.name: Ionization to Carbocation
steps.description: Identical to SN1 step 1: leaving group leaves forming carbocation. Rate-determining. Often same intermediate competes for SN1 vs E1.

steps.name: Proton Abstraction from Beta-Carbon
steps.description: Weak base removes a beta-hydrogen (on carbon adjacent to C+), electrons from C-H go to form C=C pi bond. Regioselectivity: remove H to give most substituted alkene (Zaitsev).
steps.arrow: base lone pair abstracts H+ beta to C+, C-H electrons form pi bond

sideReactions: SN1 substitution competes; ratio controlled by temperature and nucleophilicity vs basicity
mechanisms.zaitsevRule: more substituted alkene is more stable by ~6 kJ/mol per alkyl substituent due to hyperconjugation
mechanisms.howToFavour: tertiary substrate, weak base that is also nucleophile, polar protic solvent, high temperature, no strong base

mechanisms.name: E2 (Bimolecular Elimination)
mechanisms.substratePreference: tertiary > secondary > primary (still works with bulky base); primary requires bulky strong base to avoid SN2
mechanisms.base: strong, often bulky base: t-BuOK, NaOH, KOtBu, LDA; bulk favours Hoffman product (less substituted)
mechanisms.solvent: polar aprotic or protic but strong base requires aprotic or alcohol
mechanisms.stereochemistry: strict anti-periplanar required: C-H and C-X dihedral 180°; if locked cis, slower syn-elimination (rare). E/Z determined by conformation.
mechanisms.energyProfile: single concerted transition state: [B---H---C-C---X]‡ with partial double bond character
mechanisms.exampleReaction: CH3-CHBr-CH3 + KOH --EtOH, Δ--> CH2=CH-CH3 + KBr + H2O ; cyclohexane derivative requires axial-axial anti

steps.name: Concerted Anti-Periplanar Proton Abstraction and Leaving Group Departure
steps.description: Base abstracts beta-H anti to leaving group while C-X bond breaks and C=C forms simultaneously. Single transition state. Anti geometry allows good overlap of developing p orbitals to form pi bond. Hofmann vs Zaitsev selectivity: small base gives Zaitsev; bulky base gives Hofmann due to steric hindrance in accessing more substituted H.
steps.arrow: B- abstracts H, H electrons form C=C, C-X electrons leave with X-
steps.intermediate: none; requires rotamer with H and X anti (180°)
steps.stereochemistry: if diastereotopic Hs, cis alkene/trans alkene ratio reflects conformational population; anti requirement can dictate exclusive E or Z

sideReactions: SN2 competes with primary substrates and small nucleophilic bases
E1 competes with tertiary + weak base
mechanisms.howToFavour: strong bulky base, heat, hindered substrate where SN2 impossible, anti-periplanar conformation accessible

mechanisms.name: Electrophilic Addition – Alkene + HX (Markovnikov)
mechanisms.order: second order overall (first in alkene, first in HX)
mechanisms.substratePreference: more substituted alkene more nucleophilic (more stable carbocation) reacts faster: tetra > tri > di > mono > ethene
mechanisms.electrophile: polarized HX: Hδ+ - Xδ- ; H+ is electrophile
mechanisms.solvent: non-basic; often with no solvent or CH2Cl2; protic can solvate X-
mechanisms.stereochemistry: if carbocation planar, nucleophile attacks both faces -> racemate if new stereocenter; addition is not strictly syn or anti due to carbocation
mechanisms.carbocationRearrangement: yes: hydride/shift to more stable carbocation before nucleophilic capture explains anti-Markovnikov side products
mechanisms.energyProfile: two barriers: protonation to carbocation (rate-determining) then nucleophilic capture (fast)
mechanisms.conditions: no peroxide; polar HX; low temperature favours kinetic Markovnikov product

steps.name: Protonation to More Stable Carbocation (Rate-Determining)
steps.description: Pi electrons attack Hδ+ of HBr, forming C-H bond at the less substituted carbon, generating more stable carbocation at more substituted carbon. Markovnikov's rationale: proton adds to carbon that yields most substituted carbocation (hyperconjugation stabilization ~30 kJ/mol per alkyl).
steps.arrow: C=C pi bond -> H+ , H-Br electrons go to Br-
steps.intermediate: CH3-CH+-CH3 (secondary carbocation) vs alternative primary (CH3CH2CH2+); secondary favored ~40 kJ/mol

steps.name: Nucleophilic Capture by Bromide
steps.description: Br- attacks carbocation from either face. Fast, exothermic, gives final Markovnikov bromide. If bromide is weak nucleophile and water present, water can compete (halohydrin formation).
steps.arrow: Br- lone pair -> empty p orbital of carbocation

variants.name: Anti-Markovnikov (Peroxide Effect / Kharasch)
variants.condition: HBr + ROOR radical initiator -> radicals: Br· adds first to give more stable carbon radical at more substituted carbon, then H abstraction gives anti-Markovnikov CH2BrCH2CH3
variants.mechanism: radical, not carbocation; peroxide O-O homolysis ~150 kJ/mol, propagation cycle

variants.name: Acid-Catalyzed Hydration
variants.note: Water acts as nucleophile after protonation; same Markovnikov regioselectivity, deprotonation final step yields alcohol

variants.name: Halogen Addition
variants.note: Forms bromonium ion bridged intermediate, not free carbocation, leading to anti addition (opposite to HX mechanism), no rearrangement

mechanisms.howToFavour: use unbiased alkene; control peroxide presence to switch regioselectivity; keep temperature low to avoid rearrangements

mechanisms.name: Nucleophilic Addition to Carbonyl (and Grignard)
mechanisms.substratePreference: aldehyde > ketone > ester > amide (reactivity correlates with electrophilicity of carbonyl carbon; resonance donation deactivates)
mechanisms.nucleophile: hard/soft: hydride (NaBH4), cyanide, Grignard (RMgX), organolithium, acetylide, enolate
mechanisms.solvent: Grignard requires anhydrous ether (Et2O, THF) to solvate Mg2+; hydride reductions in alcohol/water
mechanisms.stereochemistry: if carbonyl attached to prochiral center, nucleophile attacks Re/Si face giving diastereomers; no inversion because sp2 trigonal planar; Felkin-Anh model predicts major diastereomer
mechanisms.energyProfile: single nucleophilic attack to tetrahedral intermediate, then protonation; Grignard has chelated transition state

steps.name: Nucleophilic Attack on Carbonyl Carbon
steps.description: Nucleophile (e.g., CH3- from Grignard or H- from hydride) attacks electrophilic carbonyl carbon (δ+) perpendicular to plane (Bürgi-Dunitz angle ~107°), pi bond electrons go to oxygen forming alkoxide tetrahedral intermediate. Carbon changes sp2->sp3.
steps.arrow: Nu- lone pair -> C=O pi* antibonding; C=O pi electrons -> O-
steps.intermediate: tetrahedral alkoxide R2C(O-)-Nu coordinated to MgBr+ if Grignard
steps.kinetics: rate-determining; ΔG‡ depends on carbonyl electrophilicity and nucleophile strength

steps.name: Protonation of Alkoxide
steps.description: Workup with aqueous NH4Cl or H3O+ protonates alkoxide to alcohol. In hydride reduction, solvent donates proton. In cyanohydrin formation, protonation yields hydroxynitrile.
steps.product: R2C(OH)-Nu : primary alcohol from formaldehyde, secondary from aldehyde, tertiary from ketone/ester (with 2 eq Grignard)

specialCases.name: Acetal Formation
specialCases.detail: 2 ROH + carbonyl --acid--> acetal via hemiacetal, reversible, water removal drives forward

specialCases.name: Reduction
specialCases.detail: NaBH4 selective for aldehyde/ketone, LiAlH4 reduces esters/acids as well

mechanisms.name: Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution (EAS) – Nitration
mechanisms.order: second order: first in arene, first in electrophile
mechanisms.substratePreference: activated rings (electron-donating: -OH, -OMe, -NH2, alkyl) faster; deactivated rings (-NO2, -CF3, -CHO) slower
mechanisms.electrophile: nitronium ion NO2+ generated from HNO3 + H2SO4 -> H2O + NO2+ + HSO4-
mechanisms.solvent: strong acid mixture (H2SO4 acts as catalyst and solvent)
mechanisms.stereochemistry: not applicable (planar aromatic); regioselectivity ortho/para vs meta defined by substituents; steric bulk reduces ortho
mechanisms.energyProfile: two barriers: pi attack to arenium ion (sigma complex, Wheland intermediate, rate-determining, loss of aromaticity ~150 kJ/mol) then deprotonation to restore aromaticity (fast, highly exothermic)

steps.name: Generation of Electrophile (Pre-equilibrium)
steps.description: Sulfuric acid protonates nitric acid, loss of water yields linear nitronium ion NO2+ (isoelectronic with CO2), very strong electrophile.

steps.name: Pi Attack to Form Arenion (Sigma Complex)
steps.description: Benzene pi electrons attack NO2+, forming tetrahedral carbon (sp3) with positive charge delocalized over 3 resonance forms (ortho/para). Loss of aromaticity, endothermic, rate-determining. Carbocation character at 3 positions.
steps.arrow: C=C pi electrons -> N of NO2+, N=O pi electrons neutralized
steps.intermediate: arenium ion / Wheland intermediate C6H6NO2+ (cyclohexadienyl cation)
steps.kinetics: slow due to aromatic stabilization energy penalty ~80 kJ/mol barrier

steps.name: Deprotonation to Restore Aromaticity
steps.description: Base HSO4- abstracts proton from sp3 carbon bearing NO2, electrons go to restore aromatic pi sextet. Highly exothermic, fast.
steps.arrow: HSO4- abstracts H+, C-H electrons reform C=C of aromatic ring

directingEffects.reason: lone pair or alkyl donation stabilizes arenium via resonance/hyperconjugation
electron-withdrawing destabilizes ortho/para arenium, meta least destabilized
inductive withdrawing but lone pairs donate via resonance stabilizing ortho/para arenium

otherEAS: Friedel-Crafts acylation (RCO+ / AlCl3, no rearrangement, deactivates after)

mechanisms.name: Free-Radical Halogenation (Alkane)
mechanisms.order: chain reaction; rate law complex 1.5 order but propagation rate ~ k[RH][X·]
mechanisms.substratePreference: hydrogen abstraction rate: tertiary > secondary > primary > methyl (BDE effect); relative rates with Cl·: 1°:3.9°, 2°:39°, 3°:164° at 25°C; tertiary selectivity higher with Br· (~1600:82:1)
mechanisms.halogen: F2 explosive unselective; Cl2 moderately selective; Br2 highly selective; I2 too slow/unfavorable (endothermic)
mechanisms.solvent: gas phase or CCl4; non-polar to avoid polar side reactions
mechanisms.stereochemistry: if chiral center radical is planar sp2 -> racemization if it remains chiral after halogenation; but most alkanes achiral
mechanisms.energyProfile: initiation homolysis X-X bond (242 kJ/mol Cl-Cl), propagation cycle with alternating exothermic/endothermic steps
mechanisms.conditions: UV light (hv) or heat 300°C, presence of radical initiator (AIBN, peroxide)
mechanisms.exampleReaction: CH4 + Cl2 --hv--> CH3Cl + HCl ; CH3-CH2-CH3 + Br2 --hv--> CH3-CHBr-CH3 (secondary, major) + CH3CH2CH2Br (minor)

steps.name: Initiation – Homolytic Cleavage
steps.description: Photon energy homolyzes weak halogen-halogen sigma bond to generate halogen radicals with one unpaired electron each. Requires hv ~350 nm for Cl2 or heat.
steps.arrow: Cl:Cl bond homolysis each Cl gets one electron -> 2 Cl·
steps.enthalpy: ΔH = +242 kJ/mol for Cl2, +193 for Br2

steps.name: Propagation Step 1 – Hydrogen Abstraction
steps.description: Chlorine radical abstracts H· from alkane, forming HCl and alkyl radical. Selectivity determined by C-H bond strength (tertiary 400 kJ/mol < primary 430 kJ/mol). Transition state has partial bond character.
steps.intermediate: alkyl radical R· (planar sp2-like, stabilized by hyperconjugation)
steps.selectivity: Br· more selective due to later, more carbocation-like transition state (Hammond postulate, endothermic H abstraction)

steps.name: Propagation Step 2 – Halogen Capture
steps.description: Alkyl radical attacks X2, abstracting X· to give alkyl halide and new halogen radical that continues chain. Very exothermic for chlorination.
steps.product: R-Cl regenerates Cl· to propagate chain (steps 2-3 cycle hundreds of times per initiation event)

steps.name: Termination
steps.description: Two radicals combine to quench chain: R·+R·->R-R, R·+Cl·->RCl, Cl·+Cl·->Cl2. Low [radical] makes this rare; product mixture includes coupling side products (ethane, polyhalogenation if excess X2).
byProducts: CCl4 from multiple chlorinations if CH4 excess Cl2

sideReactions: polyhalogenation (CH2Cl2, CHCl3, CCl4 with excess Cl2)
Russell mechanism for autoxidation with O2
mechanisms.howToControl: use excess alkane to minimize polyhalogenation, specific wavelength, tetramethylene sulfone scavenger

chirality.definition: Object non-superimposable on its mirror image; molecule chiral if it lacks an improper rotation axis (Sn), including plane of symmetry and inversion center.
chirality.criterion: Carbon with four different substituents (asymmetric carbon, stereocenter) is sufficient but not necessary; axial chirality (allenes, biphenyls) also chiral without stereocenters.
chirality.enantiomers: Pair of non-superimposable mirror images, identical physical properties except optical rotation and interaction with other chiral environments; 50/50 = racemate optically inactive.
chirality.diastereomers: Stereoisomers not mirror images; have different physical properties (mp, bp, NMR), includes cis/trans, E/Z, epimers, anomers, meso vs chiral.
chirality.meso: Achiral despite having stereocenters due to internal plane of symmetry; meso tartaric acid [2R,3S] optically inactive, possesses inversion center.
chirality.opticalActivity: Chiral sample rotates plane-polarized light: (+) dextrorotatory clockwise, (-) laevorotatory anticlockwise; specific rotation [alpha]D^20 = alpha_obs / (l * c) where l=dm, c=g/mL.

cipRules.description: Cahn-Ingold-Prelog priority assigns R/S absolute configuration at a stereocenter.

steps.rule: Assign atomic number priority to the four atoms directly attached to stereocenter; higher Z gets higher priority (I > Br > Cl > S > P > O > N > C > H). Isotopes: higher mass higher (D > H).
If tie, list atoms attached to each of those atoms in decreasing atomic number (duplicate representation for double/triple bonds: C=O counts as C bonded to O,O; C≡N as C bonded to N,N,N).
Orient molecule with lowest priority (4) to back (dashed). Trace 1->2->3; clockwise = R (rectus), anticlockwise = S (sinister).
If lowest priority is not in back, swap to make it back; each swap inverts R/S. Or use steering wheel method.
For E/Z alkenes: assign CIP priorities to the two groups on each alkene carbon; if high priorities on same side = Z (zusammen), opposite = E (entgegen).

cipRules.mnemonic: Z = same side (Zusammen = together), E = opposite (Entgegen = across)

conformation.description: Rotation about sigma bonds gives conformers not superimposable without breaking bonds.

types.name: eclipsed / staggered (ethane)
types.energy: staggered 12 kJ/mol more stable; torsional strain

types.name: gauche / anti (butane)
types.energy: anti 3.8 kJ/mol more stable than gauche; steric strain

types.name: chair / boat (cyclohexane)
types.energy: chair ~23 kJ/mol more stable than boat; 1,3-diaxial interactions

examples.name: lactic acid (2-hydroxypropanoic acid)

substituents.reason: C attached to O,O,OH > C attached to H,H,H for CH3

rIsomer.opticalRotation: (R)-lactic acid = (-)-lactic acid (some systems + rarely) ; common in literature: muscle-produced L-lactic acid is (S)
rIsomer.absoluteDescription: When H to back, OH->COOH->CH3 traces clockwise
rIsomer.biologicalOccurrence: (S)-lactic acid predominates in mammalian metabolism (LDH enzyme produces S), (R)-lactic acid produced by some bacteria
rIsomer.specificRotation: [alpha]D = -3.8° for (R), +3.8° for (S) (in water, enantiomers equal magnitude opposite sign)

sIsomer.absoluteDescription: When H to back, OH->COOH->CH3 traces anticlockwise
sIsomer.note: IUPAC L-lactic acid in older literature = S; D-lactic = R; Fischer D/L correlates but not always with R/S

examples.racemate: (RS)-lactic acid optically inactive, melting point 18°C vs enantiopure 53°C; different solubility shows diastereomeric interactions in crystal
examples.methodToAssign: Draw Fischer projection: vertical = back bonds, horizontal = forward; CIP still valid but steering rules differ

examples.name: alanine (2-aminopropanoic acid)

substituents.reason: N Z=7 > O 8? Wait O higher, but duplicate: NH2 N( H,H, lone) vs COOH C(O,O,OH) – CIP rule: compare first atom: N (7) vs C (6) vs C (6) vs H (1) => NH2 gets priority 1 actually? Check: N 7 > C 6, so NH2 > COOH, but literature assigns NH2=1, COOH=2 due to O duplicate expansion? For alanine correct order is NH2 (1), COOH (2), CH3 (3), H (4). So trace NH2->COOH->CH3.

rIsomer.commonName: D-alanine (in Fischer D/L system); rare in nature but in bacterial cell walls (peptidoglycan) and some antibiotics

sIsomer.commonName: L-alanine – proteinogenic natural enantiomer found in ribosomal translation; (S)-alanine is the standard L form
sIsomer.specificRotation: -8.5° in opposite assignment dependent on pH due to zwitterion; in neutral water [alpha]D ~ +14.5 for L
sIsomer.note: Most natural amino acids are (S) except cysteine is (R) due to sulfur priority swap, yet still L in D/L nomenclature – shows R/S ≠ D/L necessarily

examples.zwitterionNote: At physiological pH, alanine exists as CH3CH(NH3+)COO-; chirality retained, pI = 6.01

examples.name: 2-butanol

substituents.reason: C attached to C,H,H vs CH3 C attached to H,H,H – ethyl higher

rIsomer.synthesisViaSN2: Starting (R)-2-bromobutane + OH- --SN2 (inversion)--> (S)-2-butanol ; SN1 would give racemate

examples.resolutionMethod: Can be resolved via diastereomeric esters with chiral acid (e.g., tartaric acid) then fractional crystallization; enantiomers inseparable by standard chromatography but chiral GC/HPLC with cyclodextrin column separates

examples.name: tartaric acid – meso vs enantiomers

isomers.name: (2R,3R)-tartaric acid
isomers.description: Found in grapes, L-(+)-tartaric acid in old D/L notation; no plane of symmetry

isomers.name: (2S,3S)-tartaric acid
isomers.optical: laevorotatory (-12°), enantiomer of SS, mirror image

isomers.name: (2R,3S)-tartaric acid (meso)
isomers.optical: achiral meso, optically inactive, mp 165°C vs 174°C for enantiomers, has internal plane of symmetry through middle C-C bond
isomers.description: Although two stereocenters, molecule has inversion center; meso form has one R and one S which cancel. Shows different solubility and IR due to internal compensation.

examples.note: Three stereoisomers total, not four, because (R,S) identical to (S,R) identical due to symmetry – meso reduces count from 2^n=4 to 3. Demonstrates need to check symmetry before counting.

examples.cis: cis-but-2-ene = (Z)-but-2-ene: both CH3 on same side (Zusammen), bp 3.7°C, less stable, dipole 0.33 D
examples.trans: trans-but-2-ene = (E)-but-2-ene: CH3 opposite (Entgegen), bp 0.9°C, more stable by ~4 kJ/mol, dipole ~0 D
examples.assignment: CIP: on each alkene carbon, CH3 (C + H,H,H) > H (1), so Z = both high priorities same side = cis = Z, E = trans = E

examples.note: Here cis/trans terminology fails because two different halogens; must use E/Z via CIP. Assign left carbon: Cl (17) > C(CH3) (C attached to H,H,H) and right carbon: Br (35) > H. E/Z then assigned: both high (Cl and Br) same side = Z.
examples.reason: Shows why E/Z is general and cis/trans only for identical substituent pairs

examples.name: axial chirality – allenes and atropisomerism
examples.description: Even without a tetrahedral stereocenter, molecules can be chiral due to axis.

examples.chirality: Even-numbered cumulene with odd cummulated doubles gives perpendicular pi planes, substituents in perpendicular planes -> chiral axis if each end has two different substituents; enantiomers designated aR/aS

Hindered rotation about single bond due to steric bulk; if ortho substituents large enough, rotation barrier >100 kJ/mol isolates enantiomers at room temp; used in BINAP ligand for asymmetric catalysis

racemizationAndResolution.racemization: Interconversion of enantiomers via planar intermediate (carbocation, radical, enol). Heating, acid/base catalysis can racemize. SN1 gives racemization, SN2 gives inversion only.
resolutionMethods: diastereomeric salt formation with chiral resolving agent (tartaric acid, brucine) then fractional crystallization
chiral chromatography (cellulose or cyclodextrin stationary phase)
enzymatic kinetic resolution (lipase catalyzed esterification preferentially one enantiomer)
chiral derivatizing agent (Mosher's acid) to form diastereomers for NMR analysis
asymmetric synthesis using chiral catalyst (BINOL, proline) to produce excess of one enantiomer
racemizationAndResolution.enantiomericExcess: ee% = ([R]-[S])/([R]+[S]) *100%; 100% ee = pure enantiomer, 0% = racemate. Analog diastereomeric excess de%.
racemizationAndResolution.polarimetryEquation: [alpha] = alpha_obs / (l * c) ; observed rotation depends on wavelength (usually Na D-line 589 nm), temperature, solvent, concentration

spectroscopy.introduction: Spectroscopic identification uses IR for functional groups, NMR for carbon skeleton and H environment, mass spec for fragmentation. Combined they determine full structure.

ir.theory: IR absorption corresponds to vibrational modes: stretch (sym/asym) and bend. Hooke's law: wavenumber proportional to sqrt(k/mu). X-H stretches at high 2500-3700; triple bonds 2100-2300; double bonds 1600-1800; fingerprint 600-1500 highly specific.

peaks.note: H-bonded broadens to 3200-3570, polymeric broad 3200-3400

peaks.shape: extremely broad hump due to dimer H-bonding
peaks.note: Often overlaps C-H, diagnostic broad underlying C-H peaks
Dilute phenol 3600 sharp, conc broad 3200
Secondary amine single peak ~3300; tertiary no N-H
Often broad due to H-bonding in solid state
Unique high wavenumber above 3000, diagnostic for terminal alkyne
Sp2 C-H slightly higher than sp3

Conjugated ketone 1685; strained cyclic ketone higher (cyclobutanone 1780)

nmr1H.theory: Chemical shift delta ppm = (nu_sample - nu_TMS)/nu_spectrometer *1e6. TMS reference 0 ppm. Electronegative atoms deshield, anisotropy from pi systems deshields. Integration = number of protons; multiplicity = n+1 rule (J coupling); coupling constant J (Hz) reveals connectivity.
nmr1H.reference: TMS (tetramethylsilane) 0.00 ppm; CDCl3 solvent residual 7.26; DMSO 2.50; MeOD 3.31

shifts.note: Most shielded; tert-butyl singlet 1.2, very characteristic high integration (9H)
CH2 next to CH2 1.3 ppm; cyclohexane 1.43
Methine slightly deshielded
Allylic coupling small J ~1-2 Hz; acetonyl CH3 2.1
Terminal alkyne H 2.0-2.5 triplet J~2.5Hz long-range
Acetone 2.09, acetophenone 2.58
Toluene CH3 2.32, ethylbenzene CH2 2.64 quartet
CH2-Cl 3.5, CH2-Br 3.4, CH2-I 3.1, CH2-F 4.3 with large HF coupling 45Hz
CH3-O 3.3 singlet, CH2-O 3.6; CH-N shifts variable with salt formation protonation moves downfield 0.5
Diethyl ether CH2 3.38 quartet J7, methoxy 3.7
Ethyl acetate CH2 quartet 4.05, methyl ester singlet 3.66

Cis/trans distinguishing via J: trans 15-17Hz > cis 10-12Hz
Styrene vinyl 5.2,5.7,6.7
Benzene 7.27, toluene 7.1-7.2, anisole 6.8-7.2 activated ring shielding ortho/para, nitrobenzene deshielded 7.5-8.2; integrate 5H etc for substitution pattern
Very deshielded due to anisotropy and -I; aromatic aldehyde 10.0, aliphatic 9.6, doublet if alpha H

shifts.multiplicity: broad singlet, disappears with D2O exchange
shifts.note: Concentration and H-bonding dependent; phenol 4-7 intramolecular H-bonded up to 12; carboxylic acid OH 10-13 broad only visible in concentrated sample
Exchanges but often visible as sharp broad hump, concentration dependent, D2O exchangeable
Exchangeable, variable; aniline NH2 3.5 broad, amide NH 5-8 downfield due to carbonyl, pyrrole NH ~11
Unreliable low shift similar to alkane but D2O exchange
Acetylene 2.0, propargylic acetylide deshielded if conjugated

nmr1H.exchangeableProtons: OH, NH, SH, COOH exchange with D2O: shake sample with D2O -> peaks disappear, confirming exchangeable assignment. Also acid/base changes chemical shift dramatically.
nmr1H.diastereotopicNote: CH2 protons adjacent to stereocenter are diastereotopic -> ABX system, appear as two distinct doublets of doublets with geminal J~12-15 Hz, e.g., CH2OH of lactic acid 3.5 and 4.2 ppm.

nmr13C.theory: Broadband decoupled, proton-noise decoupled gives singlets per carbon; DEPT distinguishes CH3/CH2/CH/quaternary; shift range 0-220 ppm far broader than 1H, less overlap. Generally less sensitive (1.1% natural abundance) requires more scans.

massSpec.description: Molecular ion M+· determines exact mass; isotope pattern reveals halogens (Cl 3:1 M:M+2, Br 1:1), fragmentation gives structural clues via alpha cleavage and McLafferty rearrangement.

fragments.note: ethyl vs formyl indistinguishable low-res; common hydrocarbon fragment
very common base peak: propyl or acetyl (ketone). Ketones characteristic acylium 43 if CH3CO-
butyl or propionyl; tert-butyl very stable 57 strong
phenyl ion, base peak for chlorobenzene after Cl loss
Base peak for alkylbenzenes: toluene M+91, benzyl cleavage then rearranges to aromatic tropylium, very diagnostic

massSpec.isotopePattern: Cl gives M and M+2 3:1 due to 35Cl:37Cl 3:1; Br ~1:1 79Br:81Br; combined BrCl gives triple cluster; F and I monoisotopic; sulfur gives M+2 4% per S.
rules: Nitrogen rule: odd molecular weight -> odd number N (M+· odd)
Alpha cleavage: bond adjacent to heteroatom (O,N) breaks giving resonance-stabilized cation (e.g., ketones give acylium)
McLafferty rearrangement: gamma-H to carbonyl via 6-membered TS gives enol ion, common for ketones/esters/acids with gamma hydrogen
Loss of 15 (CH3), 18 (H2O from alcohol), 28 (C2H4 or CO), 29 (CHO from aldehyde), 31 (OCH3 from methyl ester) diagnostic

uvVis.description: Conjugated pi systems absorb UV, non-conjugated do not (alkane transparent >200 nm). Useful for estimating conjugation length.

absorptions.note: Visible absorption due to long conjugation -> orange color; particle-in-a-box model predicts lambda shift with length

uvVis.woodwardFieser: Rules predict lambdaMax for dienes/enones: base diene 217 nm + alkyl substituent +5, exocyclic double +5, additional conjugation +30 etc.
